I am 55 years old, farming 129 mu here in Quzhou for 40 years. I finished middle school, then went straight to the fields. My wife and I are two people at home. My son works in Handan city and sends money back, but he does not farm. With 129 mu I must use machinery services for everything — tillage, planting, harvest, spraying. I cannot do this by hand.

Right now it is early spring. My 108 mu of wheat is already in the ground, planted last October. I used Jimai 32, an improved variety. Last year this gave me 500 kg per mu, and I will not change the seed. For wheat, I already put 50 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting time — the 15-15-15 kind from Lao Zhang's input shop. Now at returning-green stage I will spread 15 kg of urea per mu, and another 10 kg urea at jointing. That works out to about 14 kg of nitrogen, 7.5 kg of phosphorus, and 7.5 kg of potassium in total per mu. I will irrigate four times: the winter irrigation is already done, then returning-green water in March, jointing water in April, and grain-filling water in May. Two pesticide sprays — one now for aphids, one later for rust. I hire a drone service, 8 yuan per mu per spray. Rotary tillage is what I use before wheat planting.

For summer maize on the same 108 mu: After wheat harvest in early June, I have maybe 10 days to plant. I use no-tillage planting with a machine — no time to plough, and I heard from the machinery driver that no-tillage maize works fine here if you get the fertilizer down. I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed — I have used this for 8 years, it is reliable. Base fertilizer is 40 kg of 15-15-15 compound per mu at planting, then 15 kg urea at big trumpet stage. That is about 13 kg nitrogen, 6 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium per mu. Three irrigations: seedling stage, big trumpet, and grain filling. Two pesticide applications for armyworm and leaf spot. I expect 600 kg per mu if the summer rains come.

My 12 mu of cotton: I plough deep in April because cotton roots need loose soil down deep. I plant hybrid cotton — the dealer pushed a new bollworm-resistant type, and my neighbor Wang Laoda tried it last year and got 260 kg per mu of seed cotton. Cotton needs heavy feeding. I put 60 kg compound fertilizer per mu as base, then 20 kg urea at first flowering. That is about 18 kg nitrogen, 9 kg phosphorus, 9 kg potassium per mu. Four irrigations: seedling, flowering, boll setting, and peak boll period. Five pesticide sprays — even with resistant varieties, I still spray for bollworm, aphids, and mites. I expect 260 kg of seed cotton per mu. The picking is the hard part — I hire 10 workers for a week in autumn, costs me a lot.

My 9 mu of millet: This plot is on the southeast corner, soil is sandier there, not good enough for wheat. I plant an improved millet variety. Millet does not need much. I put 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, that is all. About 8 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, 4 kg potassium per mu. Rotary tillage, two irrigations, one pesticide spray. Should get 280 kg per mu.

How do I decide? Three years ago our village had a meeting where they talked about using compound fertilizer together with urea. I listened and changed from using only urea. My yields went up 30 to 40 kg per mu. But I will not cut fertilizer to save money. Two years ago my nephew tried reducing nitrogen on his maize by one-third because fertilizer prices jumped. His yield dropped by 100 kg per mu. He lost more money than he saved. I would rather put a bit too much than too little — a bad harvest is a disaster. Last year compound fertilizer was 180 yuan per 50-kg bag, urea was 120 yuan. I spent nearly 80,000 yuan on fertilizer for the whole farm. It is a lot of money. But with 129 mu, I have some room to absorb costs. I watch what Wang Laoda does across the road — he farms 140 mu. If he changes his rates, I think about it. My budget is connected — spending more on fertilizer means I delay fixing my pump, but harvest comes first.
